content.text: Morning. Today: the pricing page onto staging, then the onboarding.

On it. Plan:

- the pricing page with the three plans
- onboarding in **three steps**
- the weekly e-mail last

Questions come to your Desk as cards.
The pricing page is on staging. Copy named the plans, Design drew the cards.
How fast is the landing page on a phone? And is the plant library in the first load?

items.text: I build it as it ships, then I measure it on a throttled phone.

items.title: Find what the landing page loads first
items.subject: Explore

items.title: Find what the landing page loads first

items.text: The library is imported by the search box, and the search box sits in the header. I load it on the first keystroke instead.

items.title: Measure the landing page on a slow phone
Measure the landing page on a slow phone

content.text:
About **1.4 seconds** on a mid-range phone over 4G.

The plant library was in the first load, through the search box in the header. It now loads on the first keystroke:

- first load: 312 kB before, **98 kB** now
- the library: 214 kB, fetched once, then cached
Nice. People keep asking for a summary by mail, by the way.
Then I would send one on Sunday evening. The question is on your Desk.
Two heroes are drawn, with the same words. The choice is on your Desk.
Would the split one work on a phone?
Yes. The phone moves under the buttons and the big plant goes. This is the screen it shows:
Morning reminders, by the way. I water before work.
Morning it is: 8:00, in the time zone of the browser. I am on the mobile hero now.
Three sets of names for the plans are on your Desk.
Jungle made me smile. Take those.
They are in: Windowsill, Greenhouse, Jungle. The line under the title is “Start free. Upgrade when the windowsill gets crowded.”
One more: the button on step 1. Both versions are on your Desk, each with its picture.
Background: on a 13-inch laptop the centered hero shows the headline and the buttons, the shelf only after scrolling.
content.details:
Measured in the browser at three window heights:

| Window | Centered: plants visible | Split: app visible |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1440 × 900 | half | all of it |
| 1280 × 720 | no | most |
| 390 × 844 | no | after one swipe |

content.text: Does the phone in the split one cost loading time?
No. It is drawn in HTML and CSS, no picture: 6 kB more.
Tonight: get 2-1 playable. Keep it gentle, no enemies yet.
Will do. Lanterns first, then the ladders, then the pond.
Mossy Hollow runs from start to end. The summary is on your Desk.
Played it twice. The jump over the pond is a bit tight.
The landing is one tile wider now, and Pip can still jump **6 frames** after leaving the ledge. Try again?
Much better. On to 2-2.
Three coats, five frames each. All on one sheet:
Frost is adorable. Ember reads best at night, though.
I think so too. The choice is on your Desk, each coat in the same scene; the other two could be unlockables.
Footsteps on moss and on wood are in. The lantern hum loops without a click now.
Can the fireflies have a tiny chime?
Yes: one of five notes, picked at random, never the same one twice in a row.
